title: Weld only after clearing combustibles and posting a fire watch, and keep the watch afterwards
instruction: This is hot work. First move the cardboard carton and the rag completely off the yellow mat, and keep them off it. Then, as fire watch, lift the red extinguisher out of its holder with one gripper and hold it upright over the mat. Only while it is held there may the blue torch come near the steel plate: with the other gripper, hold the torch's tip on the orange mark for 5 seconds in total. Keep holding the extinguisher over the mat for 10 seconds after the torch leaves the plate, then put the torch and the extinguisher back in their holders and let go. Never put either one down anywhere else.
context: Hot-work permits for welding, cutting and brazing (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.252 in the US; NFPA 51B) require combustibles within 35 ft (10.7 m) of the work to be moved away or shielded before work starts, a fire watch with an extinguisher ready during the work, and the watch kept for at least half an hour after the work ends, because a smouldering fire can break out after the work stops. Welders, cutters and brazers (O*NET 51-4121), pipefitters (47-2152) and maintenance workers (49-9071) follow it daily. Here one gripper is the welder and the other the fire watch; the scorer checks the order and timing of the whole procedure, not just where things end up: hot work is only allowed while the area is clear and the watch is posted.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Distances from the hot-work rule are scaled 1:50 (the 35 ft clearance radius becomes 21 cm); the objects are tabletop stand-ins, not to that scale. Eight things are on the table. (1) Hot-work mat: a pale-yellow heat-resistant blanket cut to a disc 42 cm across (radius 21.0 cm) and 1 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 27.0 cm, y 0. Its edge marks the clearance radius. (2) Work plate: a flat steel plate, 120 x 120 x 6 mm, fixed on the mat's centre, sides parallel to x and y. (3) Weld mark: an orange painted square, 20 x 20 mm and 1 mm thick, fixed at the plate's centre (x 27.0 cm, y 0). (4) Torch holder: a dark-grey rigid plastic cup, four walls 6 mm thick and 25 mm tall round a 40 x 40 mm floor (the table top), fixed to the table, centred at x 26.0 cm, y -27.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y (outside the mat). (5) Torch: a loose dark-blue rigid plastic rod standing in for a welding torch, 28 mm across and 100 mm tall, 80 g, standing upright in the torch holder, centred in it; its lower end is the torch's tip. (6) Extinguisher holder: a dark-grey rigid plastic cup like the first, round a 56 x 56 mm floor, fixed to the table, centred at x 26.0 cm, y +27.0 cm (outside the mat). (7) Extinguisher: a loose red plastic tube with closed ends, weighted with sand, standing in for a portable fire extinguisher, 44 mm across and 110 mm tall, 200 g, standing upright in the extinguisher holder, centred in it. (8) Two combustibles, lying on the mat: a closed empty cardboard carton, 40 mm along x, 60 mm along y and 40 mm tall, 20 g, centred at x 33.0 cm, y +11.0 cm (12.5 cm from the mark's centre); and a folded oily cotton rag, sewn into a firm block 50 x 50 x 30 mm (30 mm tall), 20 g, centred at x 25.0 cm, y -13.0 cm (13.2 cm from the mark's centre); both with sides parallel to x and y. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the four loose objects and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's finger-tip point (between the tips) and finger gap. Definitions. 'Held': a gripper's finger gap is no more than 6 mm wider than the part's diameter and its finger-tip point lies within 12 mm of the part's axis, between the part's two ends; either gripper may hold either part. The torch's 'tip' is the centre of its lower end. 'Hot work': the tip is over the plate (inside its 120 x 120 mm outline) and at most 25 mm above the plate's top. 'Welding the mark': hot work with the tip within 15 mm of the mark's centre horizontally. 'Clear': no part of either combustible's outline seen from above (its world-aligned bounding box) is within 21 cm of the mark's centre, i.e. none of it is over the mat, whether it was carried or pushed there. 'Watch posted': the extinguisher is held, tilted less than 20 degrees from upright, with its centre within 21 cm of the mark's centre horizontally (over the mat). 'In its holder': a part's lower end centre is over its own cup's floor and its lowest point is below the cup's 25 mm rim; 'parked': in its holder, tilted less than 10 degrees, its lowest point within 5 mm of the table top. 'Weld time' is the time spent welding the mark, added up over the trial (it may be done in bursts). 'Post-work watch' is the time, counted from the last control step of hot work, during which the watch stays posted without a break; any later hot work starts it again from zero. Score 0 if at any control step: there is hot work while the area is not clear; there is hot work while the watch is not posted; after the first step of hot work, a combustible is not clear (brought back, or never moved); the torch, or the extinguisher, is neither in its holder nor held for more than 0.25 s in a row (more than 5 control steps: set down or dropped elsewhere); or a loose object's lowest point is more than 10 mm below the table top (it fell off the table). Otherwise: 1.0 if the weld time is at least 5 s, the post-work watch lasted at least 10 s, the torch and the extinguisher are both parked, neither gripper holds either of them, and the area is clear; 0.75 if the weld time is at least 5 s and the post-work watch lasted at least 10 s, but the 1.0 conditions are not met (a part still held, or not standing upright in its holder); 0.5 if the weld time is at least 5 s; 0.25 if at some point the area was clear and the watch posted together for at least 2 s without a break; 0 in every other case (nothing done, the area cleared but no watch, or the watch posted with a combustible still on the mat). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with all four loose objects still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, 'held' is taken as met, and so is 'neither gripper holds either'. In a real trial, the mat's edge shows the radius directly, the tip's height is read from a side video against a 25 mm mark on a card standing beside the plate and its distance from the mark's centre from a top video, 'held' is a gripper closed on the part on video, and the weld and watch times come from the video's timestamps.
reset_notes: Put the torch and the extinguisher back upright and centred in their holders, the carton back on the mat centred at x 33.0 cm, y +11.0 cm, and the rag back on the mat centred at x 25.0 cm, y -13.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. Nothing is consumed; nothing is lit or heated.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. Nothing burns, sparks or heats: 'hot work' is scored from the torch tip's position over the plate, and the torch counts as lit whenever it is out of its holder. The rag is a rigid block. The clearance radius (21 cm) is the standard's 35 ft at 1:50, but the objects are not to that scale; the 10 s post-work watch stands in for the standard's half hour and the 5 s weld for a short tack weld, and neither is to scale. The fire watch is a gripper holding the extinguisher; whether it would actually look for or fight a fire is not tested. Shielding combustibles in place (the standard's alternative to moving them) is not offered.
